pairs.subject: companion-identity
pairs.evidence: characters/malakor/bible.md:219 The package does split an immutable constitution from a mutable bible, but the bible's 'Hard limits as in-world habits' table restates the constitution's red lines and, at line 219, extends red line 8 (that he may joke about being an AI). That puts a second copy of the law in the document reconcile diffs are allowed to edit, so the two copies can drift apart and an approved bible change can amend the law.

techniques.evidence: characters/malakor/bible.md:219 The partition itself is realized: constitution.md:3 says the file is immutable and only the operator changes it, and the precedence is stated inside both documents (constitution.md:80, bible.md:3). But bible.md:207-220 restates every red line, and line 219 repeats red line 8 from constitution.md:72 nearly word for word, then adds new law. The technique's one-authority rule says the mutable document may reference the constitution but must not restate it, and that a rule-shaped line in the mutable document is a constitutional edit.

characters/malakor/bible.md:144 'His tools' (bible.md:126-145) is a hand-written description of capabilities: polls, the evidence board, bone-clerk research dispatch, chat commands. Nothing in the package derives it from the list of permitted actions, and no ledger records each tool as working, broken or unexercised. A grep for unexercised/exercise-ledger vocabulary found no such ledger. Today the listed commands do match the segment tomls (seg-01: summon/propose/vote; seg-02a: hint/grade/propose/vote), so no phantom capability was found. The gap is the missing derivation and exercise record, not a wrong entry.

characters/malakor/bible.md:120 The package's model of people is a memory of many viewers on a public stream. It is not a synthesized profile of one operator, and the technique excludes agents with multiple users.

pairs.registryProposal: The subject assumes a personal companion with a self-model it writes itself. Here the closest thing to that is an operator-authored canon document (the bible) that a separate reconcile planner proposes diffs against, and the persona serves a public audience rather than one person. The golden path could say how constitution-self-model-split and anchored-identity-diffs apply when the proposer is a sibling pipeline rather than the persona itself, and when a canon file legitimately renders the law as in-fiction habits. As written, that rendering counts as a forbidden restatement, even though it is the mechanism that lets the persona refuse in character.
